summary.blockingFinding: B05 i001 Details.scenarioApplication makes an unsupported race-prevention claim; correct the explanation or expose the necessary door-policy gate/serialization in the prompt.

optionShapeAdvisory.assessment: Qualitative §4.3 review only; keys tend to enumerate protocol details while shorter distractors are often wrong-order or god-object alternatives. Assess scenario-specific plausibility without count/length thresholds.

items.beforeAcceptedMeaning: Centralize collaboration only when it removes a real many-to-many protocol without becoming a new god object. In this case, that keeps the rule “revocation is visible to the door policy before access is granted” inside the owner that can observe and enforce it.
items.currentAcceptedMeaning: Use a narrow revocation coordinator to sequence the registry, door-policy, and audit interactions while leaving each component's rules with that component.
items.rationale: The accepted answer in both versions is the same Mediator decision—centralize peer collaboration without taking over their domain rules—so preserve the question ID. However, current Details.scenarioApplication claims sequencing prevents access racing the recorded revocation, while the prompt supplies only a changing call order and the Details.boundaryOrTradeoff expressly disclaims distributed atomicity. Narrow that causal claim to consistent protocol sequencing or make the door-policy gating/serialization fact visible.
